meta.name: eval_gold_large
meta.description: Larger, topic-diverse retrieval gold set with a cross-lingual query subset. Each doc is a single, objective factual statement from public reference knowledge (HTTP RFCs, Git/OAuth/SQL/REST/TLS/Regex/JSON docs). Relevance is objective: the query's answer is literally stated in exactly one doc. The multilingual queries test cross-lingual retrieval over English docs. This set is authored for regression testing; a future externally-sourced corpus (e.g. BEIR) is the roadmap's next research step.

docs.text: HTTP 200 OK indicates the request succeeded and the server returned the requested resource.
HTTP 301 Moved Permanently tells the client the resource has a new permanent URL and to use it for future requests.
HTTP 400 Bad Request means the server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax sent by the client.
HTTP 401 Unauthorized means the request lacks valid authentication credentials for the target resource.
HTTP 403 Forbidden means the server understood the request but refuses to authorize it even with valid credentials.
HTTP 404 Not Found means the server cannot find the requested resource at the given URL.
HTTP 500 Internal Server Error indicates the server encountered an unexpected condition that prevented it from fulfilling the request.
HTTP 503 Service Unavailable means the server is temporarily unable to handle the request, often due to maintenance or overload.
The HTTP GET method requests a representation of the specified resource and should only retrieve data without side effects.
The HTTP POST method submits data to the server, commonly to create a resource or trigger a server-side process.
The HTTP PUT method replaces all current representations of the target resource with the request payload.
The HTTP DELETE method removes the specified resource from the server.
The git commit command records staged changes to the repository history along with a message describing the change.
The git branch command creates, lists, or deletes branches, which are independent lines of development in a repository.
The git merge command joins two or more development histories together by creating a new commit that combines them.
The git rebase command replays commits from one branch onto another, producing a linear history without merge commits.
The git clone command copies an existing remote repository to a new local directory, including its full history.
The git stash command temporarily shelves uncommitted changes so you can switch branches and reapply them later.
An SQL JOIN clause combines rows from two or more tables based on a related column between them, such as an INNER JOIN returning only matching rows.
An SQL index is a database structure that speeds up lookups on a table column at the cost of extra storage and slower writes.
ACID stands for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability, the four guarantees a database transaction must provide.
The OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant issues a short-lived code to the client which it then exchanges, using a client secret, for an access token.
An OAuth 2.0 scope limits what actions an access token can perform, such as read-only or write access to a protected resource.
REST requires that each request from client to server contain all the information needed to understand it, so the server keeps no client session state.
